title: Triage voice and customer bridge notes
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight runbook for:
- Rapidly standing up a communications bridge for active incidents (S1/S2).
- Producing repeatable, short-status updates for the public status page and affected customers.
- Giving on-call SREs simple, copy/paste-ready language and an internal war-room checklist to reduce cognitive load.

Scope and usage notes
- Intended for hosted API and Dedicated control-plane incidents.
- Use for incidents where customer-facing updates are needed (partial degradation or outage).
- Not a substitute for full postmortem or technical runbooks; link to those once available.
- Placeholders: replace tokens like {{INCIDENT_ID}}, {{AFFECTED_CUSTOMERS}}, {{ETA}}, {{ROOT_CAUSE}} before sending.

Quick decision matrix (which path to take)
- Sev1 (total outage or severe degradation impacting most customers): open war-room, page SRE/Eng leads, open customer bridge, schedule executive cadence, send public status updates every 15 minutes initially.
- Sev2 (partial impact to subset of customers or features): open a private bridge, update status page every 30–60 minutes, targeted customer emails/DMs.
- Sev3 (minor, background errors/no customer impact): internal note, update during incident review, no public update unless impact changes.

Roles (minimal set for a small team)
- Incident Lead: owns decisioning, high-level updates.
- Comms Lead: writes/publishes status page and customer messages.
- Tech Lead: drives triage, provides technical ETA.
- Scribe: documents timeline and public text.
- Customer Liaison / CSM: curates affected customer list and hands customer-specific notes.
- Legal/Security (optional): review if data exposure or regulatory impact.

War-room pre-flight checklist (first 5 minutes)
- Confirm incident ID and severity in Slack: #incidents -> post basic facts.
- Create bridge channel/meeting and invite roles.
- Assign scribe and comms lead.
- Quick triage: is there an obvious mitigation? If yes, implement and note step.
- Draft initial public status page message (see templates).
- Determine initial customer outreach list: hit everyone for Sev1, targeted list for Sev2.

Update cadence & structure
- Initial public update: within 10 minutes of triage start.
- Rapid cadence (Sev1): 15m updates until stabilization, then 30–60m.
- Mid/low cadence (Sev2): 30–60m updates until resolved.
- Each update should follow this simple structure:
  1) What happened (one sentence)
  2) Impact (who/what is affected)
  3) What we are doing (short bullet)
  4) ETA / next update

Status page message templates (copy/paste, keep <140 chars for headline)
- Sev1 headline: "Degraded API performance across multiple regions — investigating ({{INCIDENT_ID}})"
  Body: "We are investigating elevated latency and request errors for the Redwood API. Some customers may see timeouts or failures. Our engineers are actively investigating. Next update in 15 minutes."

- Sev2 headline: "Partial disruption affecting model inference in us-west-2 ({{INCIDENT_ID}})"
  Body: "A subset of customers using inference in us-west-2 may experience increased latency or 5xx errors. We are investigating and routing traffic where possible. Targeting next update in 30 minutes."

- Sev3 headline: "Intermittent request errors under investigation ({{INCIDENT_ID}})"
  Body: "We have observed sporadic errors in a small percentage of requests. No customer degradation for most users. Engineers are monitoring. Next update in 1 hour."

Customer email / DM starter templates (short, editable)
- Affected customer (S1/S2) — initial notification (subject): "Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — Potential impact to your Redwood inference"
  Body: "Hi {{CUSTOMER_CONTACT}},

We are currently investigating an issue affecting Redwood inference in {{REGION}} which may impact inference latency and result in request failures for some requests. Our engineering team is actively working on mitigation. We will share updates every 15–30 minutes depending on severity.

If you see production impact, please reply with example request IDs and timestamps or share logs via the secure upload link.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is disruptive and appreciate your patience.

Best,
Redwood SRE Team (on behalf of Engineering)"

- Non-impacted but interested customer — brief advisory (subject): "FYI: Investigating a platform issue ({{INCIDENT_ID}})"
  Body: "Hi {{CUSTOMER_CONTACT}},

We wanted to let you know we are investigating an issue that may affect a subset of customers. Based on current signals we do not expect impact to your account, but we will notify you if that changes.

Best,
Redwood SRE"

Executive / leadership one-liner (for slack or email brief)
- "INCIDENT {{INCIDENT_ID}} — impact: inference API degraded in us-west-2, ~X% requests returning 5xx. Engineers active, mitigation in progress; next public update in 15 mins."

Safety checks before publishing
- Confirm accuracy of affected regions/services and that the comms lead has the most recent numbers.
- Remove technical jargon unless customer is technical.
- If PII/data exposure suspected escalate to Legal/Security before any outbound comms.
- Always include next update window.

Bridging & conference etiquette
- Mute non-essential noise.
- Keep the public updates short — the bridge is for decisioning and triage.
- Scribe keeps a running timeline with messages pasted exactly as published.

Post-incident communications sequence (within 24–72 hours)
- Internal incident review note: timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigations, follow-ups.
- Public status page: update to "resolved" with a brief impact summary and link to follow-up when ready.
- Customer follow-up: targeted email to affected customers with summary, root cause (if available), and compensatory steps or credits if applicable.
- Postmortem: full write-up published to Confluence and linked from the status page or customer note where appropriate.

Postmortem comms checklist (for comms lead & incident owner)
- Draft public post-incident summary (one paragraph + bullets).
- Draft customer-facing explanation (avoid internal timeline minutiae; focus on impact and remediation).
- Coordinate with Legal/Security for wording re: data, and with BizOps for credits/refunds.
- Schedule an internal postmortem review within 7 days.

Templates for "Resolved" messages
- Short: "Resolved: API performance restored ({{INCIDENT_ID}}). We observed elevated errors between {{START}} and {{END}} impacting ~X% of requests in {{REGION}}. Root cause: {{ROOT_CAUSE}}. Follow-up: postmortem scheduled."

- Detailed: "Resolved and under investigation: We have restored service to normal levels as of {{END}}. During the incident we saw increased error rates for requests routed to a specific inference cluster. The immediate mitigation was traffic rerouting and a rolling restart. We are continuing to analyze logs and will publish a full postmortem by {{POSTMORTEM_DATE}}. If you were affected, your CSM will reach out with specific details."

Notes and iterative improvements (draft thinking)
- Try to keep first public update factual but conservative — better to under-promise on ETA than to repeatedly miss it.
- Use short, repeatable sentences to reduce editing time.
- Keep a canonical place for cut/paste snippets to avoid mistakes under stress.
- Consider tiered distribution lists so comms lead can blast appropriate groups without custom edits.

Appendix: quick copy bank (short strings)
- "Investigating"
- "Mitigation in progress"
- "Service partially degraded"
- "Service restored"
- "No customer data exposure detected"

End of draft.

Draft notes: this doc is intentionally concise and meant to be copied into incident Slack threads, the status page editor, or customer emails. Feedback requested from on-call SREs and CS leads on tone and the appropriate cadence for Sev2.
